importantNotes: Hosea's marriage to Gomer is the most dramatic prophetic action in the Old Testament.
'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' (6:6) is quoted by Jesus in Matthew 9:13 and 12:7.
The book demonstrates that God's love is unconditional — He loves even when we are unfaithful.
Hosea ministered in the final years before Israel's fall to Assyria (722 BC).
The children's names are prophetic: Jezreel (judgment), Lo-Ruhamah (no mercy), Lo-Ammi (not my people).

chapters.1: God commands Hosea to marry Gomer; their children receive prophetic names of judgment.
chapters.2: Israel's unfaithfulness rebuked; God will allure her back and restore the covenant.
chapters.3: Hosea redeems Gomer from slavery — God's love for adulterous Israel.
chapters.4: God's case against Israel — no faithfulness, love, or knowledge of God in the land.
chapters.5: Judgment on Israel and Judah for their pride and unfaithfulness.
chapters.6: 'Come, let us return to the LORD' — but their love is like a morning mist.
chapters.7: Israel's sins — political corruption, foreign alliances, pride; they do not return to God.
chapters.8: Israel has sown the wind and will reap the whirlwind — judgment for idolatry.
chapters.9: Punishment is coming; Israel will go into exile for their sin.
chapters.10: Israel is a luxuriant vine bearing bad fruit; it is time to seek the LORD.
chapters.11: God's tender love for Israel as a father loves a child — 'How can I give you up?'
chapters.12: Jacob's example; Israel must return to God and wait for Him.
chapters.13: Israel's death sentence for idolatry; but God will ransom from death.
chapters.14: A call to repentance — 'I will heal their waywardness and love them freely.'
